items.title: Single-block Gaussian-mixture separation

source.anchor: Appendix B.2.2 Proposition B.7 Eq19; Section2 normalized TV; Section3.1 Eq4 and actual mixtures; Eq20, Eq24, Ex62–Ex64 and p6.4–p6.6 / Ex65–Ex67
source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling.
source.scope: Every natural n≥3 and real κ≥4, including both endpoints and both parities.

items.statement: The actual determinant-conditioned Gaussian mixtures satisfy the full quantitative single-block TV separation. \mathrm{TV}(P_+,P_-)\ge\frac{q^n}{2+4ns/(s+1)^2}\ge\frac12\exp\!\left(-\frac{5n}{s}\right),\qquad s=\sqrt\kappa,\quad q=\frac{s-1}{s+1}. Exactly \(n\in\mathbb N,\ n\ge3\) and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge4\). No parity restriction; every \(n/2\) in the proof is real. \(\mu\) is normalized Haar probability on full \(O(n)\), with both determinant signs. The two priors are exactly twice its restrictions to \(\det O=\pm1\); \(P_\pm\) are the actual Gaussian bind mixtures defined below. TV is the normalized supremum over measurable Euclidean events. Probability, kernel measurability, finite real event mass, integrability, the selected parameter signs, Eq24 and the scalar estimates are produced internally. None is a caller hypothesis. A_O=\frac{\kappa+1}{2}I-\frac{\kappa-1}{4}(O+O^\top),\quad\gamma_O=\mathcal N(0,A_O^{-1}),\quad\nu_\pm=2\mu\!\restriction\{\det O=\pm1\},\quad P_\pm=\nu_\pm\mathrm{bind}\gamma. \begin{aligned}\delta&=\sup_{B\text{ measurable}}|P_+(B)-P_-(B)|,&s&=\sqrt\kappa,&q&=\frac{s-1}{s+1},\\a&=1-\frac1n,&r&=aq,&\ell&=\frac{4ns+(s-1)^2}{8n(n-1)},&D&=2+\frac{4ns}{(s+1)^2}.\end{aligned}
assumptions: Exactly \(n\in\mathbb N,\ n\ge3\) and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge4\). No parity restriction; every \(n/2\) in the proof is real.

\(\mu\) is normalized Haar probability on full \(O(n)\), with both determinant signs. The two priors are exactly twice its restrictions to \(\det O=\pm1\); \(P_\pm\) are the actual Gaussian bind mixtures defined below.

TV is the normalized supremum over measurable Euclidean events. Probability, kernel measurability, finite real event mass, integrability, the selected parameter signs, Eq24 and the scalar estimates are produced internally. None is a caller hypothesis.
